name: Bakbukiah
overview: Bakbukiah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically for being second among his brethren and serving as a gatekeeper. His role as a gatekeeper highlights his responsibility within the Levitical duties related to the temple or sacred spaces. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Bakbukiah means 'y-h-v-h pours out,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the outpouring or blessing of the LORD. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:17, reveals a connection to God's providence or favor.
familyAndRelationships: Bakbukiah is identified as a descendant of Levi, establishing his Levitical lineage. Scripture does not provide further details about his immediate family or other relationships beyond this tribal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Bakbukiah's significance lies in his Levitical service, particularly as a gatekeeper, a vital role in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple precincts. Being second among his brethren indicates a position of prominence or seniority within his family group. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the restoration and organization of temple worship during the post-exilic period.
